subject: Re: Performance SLO / VPC qualification — post-call follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acme.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference>
Date: 2028-05-01T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Performance SLO / VPC qualification — post-call notes and next steps

Hi Sarah — great to meet you and the Acme team today, thanks for the time. Quick recap + actionable next steps from our discovery call focused on performance/SLOs for a Private (VPC) deployment: 

Recap of targets discussed:
- Latency: target p95 end-to-end < 250 ms for standard (non-streaming) generation. For streaming responses we discussed p95 chunk latency < 100 ms.
- Throughput: steady-state ~500 QPS, with burst to 1,000 QPS during peak windows.
- Concurrency: up to 50 concurrent long-lived streaming connections.
- Typical response size: ~200–400 tokens (~3–8 KB payloads) — helps with bandwidth planning.

Network / VPC items we need from Acme NetOps:
1) Preferred connectivity: Direct Connect / Transit Gateway peering or site-to-site VPN?
2) Egress IPs or ranges to allowlist on your firewall (we will provide Redwood egress IPs once peering choice is confirmed).
3) MTU and any transit devices that might fragment traffic.
4) A traceroute / mtr from an inside-host to the proposed Redwood endpoint (we can also run probes from our side).
5) Any TLS inspection or proxy in the path that might impact streaming/TLS session keepalive.

Attachments: I attached a network diagram template and an SLO matrix that maps the targets above to monitoring checkpoints.

Next steps / owners:
- Sarah / NetOps: please share your preferred connectivity option and egress IPs, and paste a traceroute output (or authorize us to run one). (Action: Sarah)
- Redwood (Marissa): we’ll share a short streaming benchmark script and the list of IPs/ports to allow (Action: Marissa).
- Internal: Jordan, Rishi — FYI for engineering/security readiness.

Can we reconvene May 5 at 9:00 AM PT to review the traceroute and plan the peering/allowlist?

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.inference
+1 (415) 555-0199

Attachments: network-diagram.pdf (attached), slo-matrix.xlsx (attached)

From: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
Cc: Acme NetOps <netops@acme.com>
Date: 2028-05-02T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance SLO / VPC qualification — post-call notes and next steps

Hi Marissa — thanks for the thorough recap. Quick answers from NetOps side: 

- Current realistic p95 for our internal services is ~300 ms; we can invest in tuning to hit your 250 ms target depending on path and peering.
- Throughput today is around 400 QPS for similar services; we have capacity to scale to ~800 QPS with autoscaling and additional ENIs.
- We typically prefer Transit Gateway peering (AWS) for low-latency paths; we also have Direct Connect in a subset of regions.
- MTU on our VPCs is standard 1500, but we have some older appliances that rewrite packets on certain subnets — we’ll check and call that out in the traceroute.
- I’ve cc’d netops@acme.com — they’ll help with the traceroute and egress IPs.

We don’t think a site-to-site VPN is required if TGW/direct connect are options, but we can do VPN as a fallback. Also: can you share the sizing assumptions for streaming so our firewall team can estimate throughput and concurrent connections?

Sarah
Sarah Jenkins
Head of Product, Acme Corp
sarah.jenkins@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acme.com>, Acme NetOps <netops@acme.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference>
Date: 2028-05-03T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance SLO / VPC qualification — post-call notes and next steps

Thanks Sarah — that all helps. A few clarifications and what we’ll send over this week: 

Network / perf guidance (recommended):
- Preferred: Transit Gateway / Direct Connect for lowest jitter and predictable path. VPN ok as fallback but expect slightly higher p95.
- MTU: 1500 is fine; please flag any subnets with intermediate proxies that do TLS termination/inspection.
- Internal latency budget: to meet p95 < 250 ms end-to-end we recommend keeping internal one-way latency < 25–30 ms from your app tier to the Redwood ingress.
- Ports: outbound 443 (TLS) is required for our managed connections; we only use mutual TLS for workloads that require client certs (let us know if you require that).

Streaming sizing (for firewall/throughput):
- Each live streaming connection typically sustains small chunked messages (~1–4 KB per chunk) at up to ~20 chunks/sec in high-throughput scenarios.
- For 50 concurrent streaming connections and bursts to 1,000 QPS, plan for ~100–150 Mbps sustained with headroom for bursts (depends on average chunk size).

I’m attaching an SLO matrix that maps targets to tests we’ll run (latency/throughput/concurrency). I’ll also drop a short curl-based streaming example and a small benchmark script to a shared Drive link after this email.

Action items: 
- NetOps (Acme): please share traceroute outputs and egress IPs (Action: netops@acme.com).
- Redwood (Marissa): we’ll share IP allowlist + streaming test script + expected ephemeral ports.
- Schedule: confirm May 5 9:00 AM PT for a short sync to review traceroute and peering next steps.

Thanks — Marissa

Attachments: slo-matrix.xlsx (attached)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acme.com>, Acme NetOps <netops@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference>
Date: 2028-05-05T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance SLO / VPC qualification — post-call follow-up

Hi Sarah / NetOps — Jordan here from Redwood infra. Quick internal note and offer: we can spin up synthetic probes from our private deployment to your proposed VPC endpoint to validate latency/jitter before cutover.

What we need from you to run probes:
- Target IP(s)/hostname and any NAT/allowlist IP(s) on your side.
- Confirmation which peering method you prefer (TGW / Direct Connect / VPN).
- Preferred time window for a short probe run (we can do 30 min windows during off-peak).

Rishi (cc) will handle any security/compliance Qs (mTLS, allowed ciphers, audit logging).

I’ll be on the May 5 sync — looking forward to seeing the traceroute and next steps.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Infra Lead, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.inference
